I have been a teacher for many years and in all those years, there are two events that I remember very clearly. The first was back when I was a new, young teacher and I was assigned to teach a class of children with many behavioral issues. These children were so challenging for me that I was on the verge of burning out. I could not find any manageability in the classroom. Everything I tried seemed to have little to no effect. The more I tried, the more exhausted I became both mentally and physically. There was one day, I was so tired, I could not stand to be in the classroom. I was dreading going in. As I sat in my car, I prayed silently for guidance. Suddenly, in the stillness of my soul, I felt a deep peace wash over me like a warm wave. I didn’t understand where it came from or how it happened but it was the most precious feeling I had ever experienced. It seemed to fill me with an energy that lifted me up and filled me with hope. When I entered the classroom, it was like I entered a room where a single light was shining just on me. I couldn’t see the students, but I could see everything else. The board seemed to be almost glowing as if it was just for me. The students’ faces were peaceful and I didn’t care if they were behaving or not. It was the most peaceful, and I was so happy in that state. When the bell rang, it was still one of the most precious moments of my life. I wish I could have carried that feeling every day afterwards. I didn’t understand the source of it then, but I know it was a gift. One of the things that is so fascinating to me, is how we as humans, can have such a deep need to be understood, to be heard, to be known that it can break us. Yet, when we actually take the time to listen, to hear, it can be a healing balm to the soul. I remember another time this happened. I was in the process of closing up my classroom for the day and gathering up all the things I had taught. I was emotional about this, and probably more than I should have been but it was a necessary closing of a chapter in my life. I needed to feel that I had done something... Why did the author feel like she had "been blessed"? - not enough information - Because she was given a gift of peace in her classroom - Because the students were behaving well - Because she was promoted
(Answer)
Because she was given a gift of peace in her classroom
